input.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
input.rationale: Section 13 (p0090) contains a Vendor-side IP indemnity: Garman warrants it owns or controls all rights necessary to grant the licence and free of encumbrances, and indemnifies Sparkling (and its officers and directors) for all Losses — expressly including court costs, arbitration fees, settlement amounts and reasonable legal fees — arising from breach of that warranty, which is the operative third-party IP infringement risk. The standard remedy ladder is present at p0091–p0093 (procure the right to use, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify), and the clause survives termination (p0131). The indemnity sits at the fallback: it carries no Customer-modification, combination or specification exclusions (more favourable to us than the fallback tolerates), and Section 15 expressly provides that "The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14." (p0105), so Garman's indemnity exposure is uncapped rather than limited to a 3× annual-fee super-cap — again better than the fallback. There is no reciprocal Sparkling indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, so the walk-away risk of a one-way customer indemnity does not arise. Two points short of our preferred position are noted but not redlined: there is no express duty to defend (recovery is on an indemnify/hold-harmless basis) and no separate refund remedy if none of (a)–(c) is achievable — though the uncapped recovery of all Losses and direct damages for a Section 13 breach materially covers that outcome, and the Section 7/8 rejection mechanic returns all amounts paid in the pre-acceptance window. The ten calendar day notice requirement is tighter than we would prefer but is anchored to a responsible officer's awareness and is not expressed as a forfeiture condition; we would accept it as drafted.
